about: Shared weekly MCQ bank. Written by tools/weekly-mcqs.mjs from the app guideline text, checked by the server, approved by merging the weekly pull request. One question per line.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with a lesion confined to the distal (penile) urethra. Which histologic type is most likely for this location?
questions.explain: Distal/anterior urethral tumours are commonly squamous, as stated in the histology section.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man undergoing trans‑urethral resection of a prostatic urethral tumour is found to have invasion into the prostatic stroma. What is the correct T stage for this finding?
questions.explain: Prostatic urethral T2 denotes invasion into the prostatic stroma according to the staging description.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old patient with urethral carcinoma is found to have a single inguinal lymph node metastasis (N1). According to the 2026 pathway, what is the recommended overall treatment strategy?
questions.explain: Node‑positive disease generally requires multimodal therapy rather than surgery alone, as outlined in the 2026 staging/histology‑specific pathway.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with a superficial (T1) distal urethral carcinoma without nodal involvement. Which surgical principle is appropriate for this lesion?
questions.explain: Distal superficial disease can be managed with urethra‑preserving excision ensuring negative margins, per the local/nodal treatment guidance.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a penile squamous cell carcinoma invading the corpus spongiosum without urethral involvement. According to the UICC/AJCC TNM classification, how is the primary tumour correctly staged?
questions.explain: T2 denotes invasion into the corpus spongiosum ± urethra, whereas T3 involves the corpus cavernosum. T1b represents subepithelial connective tissue invasion with adverse features.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man undergoes radical inguinal lymphadenectomy for penile squamous cell carcinoma. Pathology reveals 4 positive inguinal nodes with extranodal extension (ENE). What is the recommended further surgical management?
options: Observation alone since the inguinal nodes have been fully excised
Prophylactic ipsilateral pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND)
Bilateral prophylactic groin irradiation without pelvic surgery
Immediate systemic chemotherapy without further pelvic staging
questions.explain: EAU guidelines recommend prophylactic ipsilateral PLND when ≥3 inguinal nodes are positive or ENE is present. Observation is insufficient given the high-risk pelvic recurrence profile.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man presents with fixed, bulky inguinal lymphadenopathy (cN3) from penile squamous cell carcinoma and is chemotherapy-fit. Which of the following is the best-established prospective cisplatin- and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimen?
questions.explain: TIP is the best-established prospective cisplatin/taxane neoadjuvant regimen for cN3 disease, whereas TPF has more limited prospective evidence and substantial toxicity.

questions.stem: During multidisciplinary review of a pathology report for penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN), a resident asks about routine histological grading. According to ISUP 2025 guidance cited in the EAU guidelines, what is recommended regarding PeIN?
options: PeIN must be routinely graded as low, intermediate, or high grade
PeIN should not be routinely graded
PeIN grading is mandatory only if lymphovascular invasion is present
PeIN is graded using the same criteria as verrucous carcinoma
questions.explain: ISUP 2025 specifically advises not routinely grading PeIN itself. Distractors incorrectly suggest mandatory grading schemas.

questions.stem: A pathologist evaluates an HPV-associated penile squamous cell carcinoma variant. Which of the following serves as the practical surrogate marker for HPV-related pathway biology?
questions.explain: p16 IHC is noted as the practical surrogate marker for HPV-related pathway biology in HPV-associated SCC variants. Ki-67 or E-cadherin are not cited as HPV surrogates in this context.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman is diagnosed with Bladder Pain Syndrome (BPS). During cystoscopy, circumscribed reddened mucosa with small vessels radiating to a central scar that bleeds on distension is noted. How is this specific subtype classified?
questions.explain: Hunner lesion (ulcer) subtype is classified as ESSIC type 3C, which features circumscribed reddened mucosa with radiating vessels. Glomerulations and non-Hunner subtypes are distinct and do not represent this specific lesion.

questions.stem: Which of the following findings after hydrodistension of the bladder is known to be non-specific, not diagnostic for BPS, and frequently found in asymptomatic women?
questions.explain: Glomerulations are petechial haemorrhages after hydrodistension that are not specific or diagnostic, as they can be found in asymptomatic women. Hunner ulcers are distinct inflammatory lesions, not merely post-distension hemorrhages.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with BPS and pelvic floor tenderness is being educated on physical therapy options. Which intervention should be specifically avoided as it can worsen her pain?
questions.explain: Kegel strengthening exercises can worsen pelvic floor pain and should be avoided in BPS with pelvic floor tenderness. Manual myofascial release and trigger-point therapy are the recommended physical therapy approaches.

questions.stem: A patient taking pentosan polysulfate (PPS) for BPS requires specific long-term monitoring due to the risk of which complication?
questions.explain: Pentosan polysulfate causes a pigmentary maculopathy, necessitating a baseline eye examination and regular retinal checks during treatment. The other complications are not linked to PPS in the guidelines.

questions.stem: According to EAU guidelines, which of the following treatments must NOT be used in the management of BPS?
questions.explain: Intravesical BCG is explicitly listed among treatments that must not be used (along with long-term oral antibiotics and others). Intravesical hyaluronic acid and cyclosporine A are accepted options for therapy.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old male with treatment-resistant hypertension and persistent hypokalaemia is found to have an incidental 1.5 cm adrenal mass. Which hormonal test is specifically indicated for this clinical phenotype?
questions.explain: An aldosterone/renin ratio is indicated when an incidentaloma patient is hypertensive or hypokalaemic to screen for primary aldosteronism. The 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test is recommended for every patient universally rather than being triggered by this specific phenotype.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female undergoes a CT scan for flank pain, revealing a homogeneous 2.5 cm left adrenal mass measuring 15 HU on unenhanced CT. What is an appropriate management option according to guidelines?
options: Core needle biopsy without prior biochemical testing
Immediate surgical adrenalectomy for presumed adrenocortical carcinoma
questions.explain: For a homogeneous mass measuring 11-20 HU and under 4 cm, options include immediate further imaging or repeating unenhanced CT in 12 months. Open en-bloc resection is reserved for suspicious or malignant masses like ACC, not for small 15 HU lesions.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old patient is diagnosed with a resectable adrenocortical carcinoma. What is the standard surgical approach for this condition?
options: Core needle biopsy followed by active surveillance
questions.explain: Open en-bloc oncologic resection is the standard surgical approach for resectable adrenocortical carcinoma. Minimally invasive enucleation is inadequate and discouraged due to oncologic principles.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old presents with a 4 cm heterogeneous left adrenal mass and episodic headaches with palpitations. Before scheduling a core needle biopsy, what must be ruled out?
questions.explain: A pheochromocytoma must be excluded before biopsying any potentially functional adrenal mass because biopsy of a pheochromocytoma can precipitate a dangerous catecholamine crisis. Other functional entities do not present the same acute procedural crisis risk from a needle biopsy.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old asymptomatic female undergoes a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test for a 2 cm right adrenal incidentaloma. Her post-test serum cortisol level is 65 nmol/L without overt Cushing signs. How should this result be classified?
questions.explain: A post-dexamethasone cortisol level greater than 50 nmol/L without overt Cushing syndrome indicates mild autonomous cortisol secretion, prompting screening for hypertension, diabetes, and bone disease. Values equal to or below 50 nmol/L effectively exclude autonomous secretion.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old undergoes staging for high-grade UTUC. Imaging reveals tumour invasion into the peripelvic fat. According to the TNM classification, how is this stage categorized?
questions.explain: Tumour invasion into peripelvic or periureteric fat or renal parenchyma is classified as T3, whereas T2 involves the muscularis and T4 involves adjacent organs.

questions.stem: Which of the following histological variants in upper-tract urothelial carcinoma specifically increases the concern for systemic spread and may favour radical management?
questions.explain: Micropapillary, plasmacytoid, and sarcomatoid variants are aggressive differentiations that increase concern for systemic spread and favour radical management.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old presents with advanced metastatic upper-tract urothelial carcinoma. According to contemporary EAU guidelines, what is the preferred first-line systemic regimen regardless of cisplatin eligibility?
options: Gemcitabine and carboplatin followed by avelumab maintenance
questions.explain: Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab is the preferred first-line regimen for advanced urothelial carcinoma based on EV-302, regardless of cisplatin eligibility.

questions.stem: Following radical nephroureterectomy for high-risk UTUC, which postoperative systemic intervention is supported by the POUT trial to improve disease-free outcomes?
questions.explain: The POUT trial supports adjuvant gemcitabine-platinum chemotherapy after RNU in appropriately staged high-risk UTUC to improve disease-free outcomes.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old undergoes kidney-sparing endoscopic treatment for low-grade UTUC. Which of the following is a key management requirement regarding this modality?
options: It requires intensive second-look ureteroscopy and imaging due to high recurrence rates
It is considered a definitive one-and-done therapy that eliminates follow-up needs
It is routinely sufficient for high-grade invasive tumours without further intervention
It must always be combined with upfront radical nephroureterectomy
questions.explain: Endoscopic treatment requires complete or near-complete ablation and intensive follow-up because recurrence is common, meaning it is not a one-and-done therapy.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with recurrent UTIs and post-void dribbling. Examination reveals a tender anterior vaginal mass. Which treatment approach is indicated for this symptomatic female urethral diverticulum?
questions.explain: Symptomatic urethral diverticula should be treated with transvaginal diverticulectomy, whereas asymptomatic small ones may be observed. Endoscopic fulguration or antibiotics alone are insufficient for complete resolution of the outpouching.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman undergoes complex transvaginal urethral diverticulectomy. To prevent poor healing and tissue breakdown due to a large defect, which tissue reinforcement technique is recommended?
options: Use of a synthetic mid-urethral sling
questions.explain: A Martius flap should be used if tissue is poor or the defect is large during urethral diverticulectomy. Synthetic mid-urethral slings are strictly contraindicated when addressing coexisting SUI with a diverticulum due to erosion risks.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with chronic urinary retention due to detrusor underactivity requires long-term bladder management. Which of the following is considered the safest long-term bladder drainage method?
questions.explain: Clean intermittent self-catheterisation (CISC) is the safest long-term drainage method to protect the bladder in chronic retention, while long-term indwelling catheters should be avoided where possible.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman develops severe bladder outlet obstruction 4 weeks after undergoing a pubovaginal sling procedure. What is the most appropriate management step at this early stage?
options: Initiation of clean intermittent self-catheterisation indefinitely
Immediate total excision of the entire mid-urethral mesh
questions.explain: For early post-sling obstruction within about 2 to 6 weeks, the proper management is to loosen or incise the sling. Total mesh excision or delayed urethrolysis are reserved for later presentations.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents with a congenital Hutch diverticulum located at the ureterovesical junction. What is the characteristic anatomical feature and potential complication associated with this specific lesion?
options: It arises secondary to severe iatrogenic urethral strictures and causes urinary retention.
It occurs at the ureterovesical junction and may cause vesicoureteric reflux.
It is always lined by adenocarcinoma and requires immediate radical cystectomy.
It develops exclusively from Skene's gland infections and produces post-void dribbling.
questions.explain: A congenital Hutch diverticulum occurs specifically at the ureterovesical junction and may cause reflux. It is distinct from acquired outlet-obstruction diverticula and Skene's gland pathology.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman presents with severe pelvic pressure and difficulty emptying her bladder. Examination reveals complete eversion of the vagina, with the most distal point measuring at least tvl - 2 cm. What is her POP-Q stage?
questions.explain: Stage IV POP-Q is defined by complete eversion of the vagina, reaching at least tvl - 2 cm. Stage III requires the most distal point to be more than 1 cm beyond the hymen but less than tvl - 2 cm.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman with stage III uterine prolapse and elevated post-void residual urine has recurrent urinary tract infections. According to the EAU guidelines, which investigation is specifically indicated to evaluate the upper urinary tract?
questions.explain: A renal ultrasound is indicated for stage III-IV prolapse with raised PVR, voiding difficulty, or recurrent UTI to rule out hydronephrosis. Intravenous urogram is not the recommended first-line imaging in this guideline.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is diagnosed with symptomatic stage II cystocele and rectocele. She desires a non-surgical approach to improve her symptoms. What is the recommended duration for supervised pelvic floor muscle therapy (PFMT)?
questions.explain: Supervised PFMT for at least 16 weeks is recommended for symptomatic stage I-II prolapse. Shorter durations like 4 or 8 weeks are insufficient to achieve the guideline-specified trial.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman undergoes abdominal sacrocolpopexy using lightweight polypropylene mesh for recurrent vault prolapse. Which of the following is a known risk of this procedure that occurs at a higher rate when combined with a total hysterectomy?
questions.explain: Mesh exposure is a known risk of sacrocolpopexy, and its rate is higher when the procedure is combined with a concurrent total hysterectomy. Ureteral transection is a general pelvic surgery risk, not specifically elevated by total hysterectomy in this context.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with a vaginal bulge and heaviness. Which of the following symptoms is considered the most specific for pelvic organ prolapse?
questions.explain: Vaginal bulge or heaviness is explicitly highlighted in the guidelines as the most specific symptom of pelvic organ prolapse. While urgency and sexual dysfunction can occur, they are less specific to prolapse alone.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man undergoes a work-up for painless gross hematuria. Cystoscopy reveals a suspicious flat red patch, but multiple random biopsies are negative. Urine cytology shows high-grade urothelial carcinoma cells. According to the guidelines, what is the most appropriate next clinical step?
options: Evaluation of bladder CIS, upper tract and prostatic urethra
questions.explain: A positive cytology with a negative cystoscopy specifically triggers evaluation of bladder CIS, upper tract and prostatic urethra. Immediate radical cystectomy is premature without confirming the site and extent of disease.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old patient with BCG-naïve high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer is planned for full-dose BCG induction. Which novel immunotherapy can be discussed as an addition to BCG based on recent EAU guideline updates?
questions.explain: In BCG-naïve high-risk disease, adding durvalumab or sasanlimab to BCG induction and maintenance can be discussed to improve disease-free survival. Pembrolizumab is used in other settings like BCG-unresponsive disease.

questions.stem: According to UICC TNM 9 classification for bladder cancer, what does a T3b stage designation indicate?
options: Tumour invades the inner half of the muscle layer
questions.explain: Under TNM 9, T3a indicates microscopic perivesical tissue invasion, whereas T3b represents macroscopic perivesical invasion. T2a covers the inner muscle and T4a invades the prostatic stroma.

questions.stem: Following response or stable disease after 4 to 6 cycles of first-line platinum combination chemotherapy for metastatic urothelial carcinoma, what is the established standard maintenance therapy?
questions.explain: Maintenance avelumab is established following response or stable disease after 4-6 cycles of platinum combination therapy based on JAVELIN Bladder 100. Pembrolizumab is used in other lines, not as post-platinum maintenance.

questions.stem: During an active regional shortage of bacillus Calmette-Guerin, how should departments appropriately prioritize patients for intravesical treatment according to the guidelines?
options: Give full induction to all intermediate-risk patients first
Switch all patients directly to intravesical chemotherapy
questions.explain: During a BCG shortage, guidelines specifically advise prioritizing high-risk patients and utilizing local reduced-dose or frequency protocols. Low-risk patients should not take precedence over high-risk disease.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man undergoes an mpMRI for an elevated PSA. His imaging reveals a PI-RADS 3 lesion, and his PSA density is calculated at 0.08 ng/mL^2. With low clinical suspicion, what is the guideline-suggested approach regarding biopsy?
options: Mandatory repeat mpMRI in 3 months before biopsy
questions.explain: For PI-RADS 3 lesions with a PSA density <0.10, EAU guidelines note this is a very-low-risk setting where surveillance can be considered rather than immediate biopsy. Immediate biopsy is recommended for higher PI-RADS scores or higher PSA densities.

questions.stem: A prostate needle biopsy shows three distinct architectural patterns: Gleason pattern 3 (most common by extent), pattern 4, and pattern 5 (highest grade, present in a small focus). According to biopsy Gleason scoring rules, how should this be scored?
options: Most common plus second most common pattern (3+4)
Most common plus highest grade regardless of extent (3+5)
Entirely determined by the percentage of pattern 4
The highest grade doubled as the primary and secondary score (5+5)
questions.explain: When three patterns are present on a biopsy, the scoring rule requires recording the most common pattern plus the highest grade pattern, regardless of its extent. Scoring the second most common would miss higher-grade elements.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with localized prostate cancer, clinical stage cT2a, PSA of 14 ng/mL, and a biopsy showing ISUP Grade Group 2 (Gleason 3+4). According to the EAU 2026 risk classification, what is his risk group?
questions.explain: Under EAU 2026 criteria, unfavorable intermediate risk includes GG2 with a PSA of 10-20 ng/mL, whereas favorable intermediate risk requires GG2 with PSA <10 or GG1 with PSA 10-20.

questions.section: 6. mHSPC • doublet • triplet • emerging biomarker-driven therapy
questions.stem: A patient with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) is found to have tumor PTEN deficiency. Based on recent guideline-cited targeted approvals, which combination is appropriate for this molecular profile?
questions.explain: Capivasertib combined with abiraterone is indicated for PTEN-deficient mHSPC based on trial data (CAPItello-281), whereas options like olaparib or niraparib primarily target HRR/BRCA mutations.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) experiences a rapid PSA doubling time of 6 months while on continuous ADT. Which of the following is a guideline-supported ARPI option to add for high-risk nmCRPC?
questions.explain: For M0 CRPC at high risk of metastasis (PSA-DT <10 months), approved ARPI options include darolutamide, apalutamide, or enzalutamide. Chemotherapy is not the standard first-line choice for high-risk nmCRPC.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old asymptomatic patient is found to have a cystic renal lesion with enhancing thick, irregular septa, classified as Bosniak III. What is the recommended management approach?
options: Immediate radical nephrectomy in all cases
Individualized management with surveillance or surgery depending on size, age and risk
Routine annual ultrasound without further imaging
questions.explain: Bosniak III lesions have a substantial malignancy risk, but management is individualized using surveillance or surgery based on size, age, and risk rather than automatic radical surgery. Routine ultrasound alone is inadequate for surveillance.

questions.stem: During staging of a renal cell carcinoma, imaging reveals tumor thrombus extending into the inferior vena cava (IVC) below the diaphragm. How is this classified under the TNM system?
questions.explain: T3b is defined as tumor thrombus extending into the IVC below the diaphragm. T3a involves the renal vein/segmental branches, pelvicalyceal system, or perirenal fat.

questions.stem: Following disease progression on a first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor combination for metastatic clear-cell RCC, a patient is evaluated for subsequent therapy. Which of the following approaches is explicitly advised against by EAU guidelines?
options: Using cabozantinib or another unused VEGFR-TKI
Re-challenging with an ICI combination based on CONTACT-03 trial data
Administering belzutifan alone after prior PD-(L)1 and VEGFR-TKI
questions.explain: The CONTACT-03 trial was negative, and guidelines explicitly state not to re-challenge with an ICI. VEGFR-TKIs and belzutifan options remain valid standard pathways.

questions.stem: A pathologist reviews a clear-cell renal cell carcinoma specimen and notes extreme pleomorphism and sarcomatoid morphology. According to WHO/ISUP grading standards, what grade should be assigned?
questions.explain: WHO/ISUP grade 4 includes extreme pleomorphism, sarcomatoid, or rhabdoid morphology. Grades 1 to 3 reflect varying degrees of nucleolar prominence.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old asymptomatic patient is diagnosed with localized clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (cT1b N0). Which of the following staging strategies regarding bone and brain metastases is supported by current guidelines?
options: Routine bone and brain CT must be performed for all newly diagnosed patients
Bone and brain imaging should be targeted to symptoms, stage, and systemic-treatment context rather than performed routinely
Routine cranial MRI is mandatory prior to partial nephrectomy
Bone scintigraphy is required for every patient with a renal mass >3 cm
questions.explain: Routine bone or brain imaging is not required for every asymptomatic RCC patient and should instead be targeted to symptoms, stage, and the systemic-treatment context. Routine mandatory scans for all patients are not recommended.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man presents with a solid testicular mass identified on ultrasound. When should serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, and LDH) be evaluated relative to radical inguinal orchiectomy?
options: Mandatory before orchiectomy and repeated after orchiectomy
Only before orchiectomy to establish baseline values
Only after orchiectomy once final histology is confirmed
Delayed until staging CT scans are completed
questions.explain: Tumor markers are mandatory before orchiectomy and must be repeated after orchiectomy because clinical staging and prognosis depend heavily on post-orchiectomy values. Evaluating them only preoperatively misses marker kinetics.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man undergoes radical orchiectomy for a pure seminoma, but his postoperative serum AFP remains persistently elevated. How should this patient be managed?
options: Manage as a nonseminoma regardless of the dominant histology
Treat as pure seminoma with adjuvant carboplatin AUC 7
Repeat serum markers every 3 months while on surveillance
Administer adjuvant radiotherapy to the retroperitoneum
questions.explain: AFP should not be elevated in pure seminoma; if AFP is persistently elevated after orchiectomy, the case must be managed as a nonseminoma regardless of dominant histology. Surveillance or radiotherapy would be inappropriate.

questions.stem: According to the IGCCCG metastatic risk classification, which of the following accurately describes metastatic seminoma risk grouping?
options: Seminoma is good risk when no non-pulmonary visceral metastasis is present, and intermediate risk when non-pulmonary visceral metastasis is present
Seminoma includes a distinct poor-risk category when LDH exceeds 10 times the upper limit of normal
Metastatic seminoma is always classified as intermediate risk regardless of metastatic sites
Seminoma with lung metastases is automatically classified as poor risk
questions.explain: Seminoma is classified as good risk when no non-pulmonary visceral metastasis is present and intermediate risk when non-pulmonary visceral metastasis is present. There is no poor-risk seminoma group in the IGCCCG classification.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with metastatic NSGCT achieves normalized tumor markers after chemotherapy, but a visible residual mass measuring 1.5 cm remains in the retroperitoneum. What is the standard next management step?
options: Routine 18F-FDG PET/CT to differentiate fibrosis from viable cancer
Active surveillance with serial CT imaging every 3 months
Salvage chemotherapy with VIP regimen for 4 cycles
questions.explain: With normalized or normalising markers, a visible residual mass greater than 1 cm generally requires post-chemotherapy RPLND. PET is not relied upon to rule out NSGCT residual disease.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is diagnosed with stage IIA seminoma. Which of the following represents an acceptable guideline-supported treatment option?
options: Routine post-chemotherapy RPLND as primary therapy
questions.explain: Options for seminoma IIA/B include radiotherapy (IIA 30 Gy, IIB 36 Gy), BEP x3 / EP x4, or primary nerve-sparing RPLND in expert centers for marker-negative disease. Single-dose carboplatin and single-cycle BEP are options for stage I disease.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man undergoes a frequency-volume chart for nocturia. What nocturnal urine volume percentage of the 24-hour volume defines nocturnal polyuria in older adults?
questions.explain: In older adults, nocturnal polyuria is defined as a nocturnal urine volume above about 33% of the 24-hour volume, whereas 20% applies to young adults.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old smoker presents with urinary urgency and microscopic haematuria. What is the mandatory next step to rule out carcinoma in situ?
questions.explain: Urgency with haematuria requires cystoscopy and cytology to screen for carcinoma in situ. Ultrasound is insufficient for mucosal lesions.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman with OAB is being evaluated for a new prescription of mirabegron. Which baseline condition mandates avoiding this drug?
questions.explain: Mirabegron can increase blood pressure and should be avoided in patients with severe uncontrolled hypertension. Controlled hypertension is not a strict contraindication.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with refractory idiopathic OAB is considering intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U. Which key prerequisite must be confirmed before treatment?
options: Willingness and ability to perform clean intermittent self-catheterisation
Normal post-void residual urine volume under 50 mL
questions.explain: Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA carries a 5-10% risk of urinary retention requiring clean intermittent self-catheterisation, so the patient must be willing and able to perform it.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with nocturnal polyuria is prescribed low-dose sublingual desmopressin. What is the licensed starting dose for men?
questions.explain: The licensed low-dose oral or sublingual starting dose of desmopressin for nocturnal polyuria is 50 g in men and 25 g in women.
